I reviewed the flag against the draft text and the checklist.

**Flag 1 — "would have produced an average annual return of 8.7%"**

The sentence presents a 26-year backtested result for the Four-Bucket Income Model with a single return figure and no fee characterization anywhere in the piece. Nothing in the surrounding paragraph, the "Important Information" block, or any footnote states whether advisory fees and expenses were deducted, and no companion net figure appears at all — let alone with equal prominence. A model run "against actual market returns" would ordinarily be computed before advisory fees unless stated otherwise, so the reader is left with the more favorable of the two numbers. That is squarely the kind of text a reviewer should pull, so the flag is well-founded.

It is not a duplicate of anything on the unmatched list, since that list is empty.

Worth noting for the reviewer's benefit (beyond the flag as written): the same sentence carries additional exposure the first-pass reviewer did not call out — it is backtested/model performance presented without the criteria, assumptions and limitations of the backtest (C5), it pairs a return with a "no calendar year worse than -4.1%" drawdown claim that would need substantiation (C6), and it omits standard 1-, 5- and 10-year period presentation (C3). The C2 point stands on its own, but the paragraph likely needs broader rework than a net-of-fee figure alone.
